propositions: Per-pair overlap judgment issues 2N calls for N candidates; batching N candidates per call reduces this to 2*ceil(N/batch) calls, eliminating redundant system-prefix transmissions.

The cached prefix (system block: base prompt + hoisted query digest) reaches the 1024-token floor only when the batch-protocol section is added to the system prompt, not by putting more candidates in the user message.
Batching reduces total input tokens by 48% (17,558→9,116 on a 6-candidate corpus) versus pre-8415 baseline, and enables prefix caching (write 1,331 then read 1,331) that was previously unachievable.

Judgment relation labels shift systematically on 6/12 ordered pairs when batching is applied versus per-pair judgment, with a bias toward conservative (downgrading weak directional claims to unrelated), but true-positive recall on injected self-duplicate remains intact.
Demultiplexing by candidate label rather than response position ensures one verdict per candidate; missing or unknown batch entries abstain only that candidate without propagating errors.
The change stacks on ticket 8415 (which hoisted the query digest to the system prompt) and requires no config changes, schema additions, or parallelization of cold calls.
